case.summary: The customer reported a $482.12 purchase they did not make, triggering an investigation of four online purchases between $400 and $500 that occurred within 30 minutes on the same card. The evidence shows a repeated under-$500 run shape that also appears on 11 other cards within ±30 days, indicating a coordinated scheme, and an earlier investigation had already linked this card to fraud. The case was escalated to a fraud analyst, who confirmed the pattern and agreed it is fraudulent. The card was blocked and the case was created, with connected cards being monitored and a report filed. The analyst was consulted as requested and confirmed the findings.

sar.narrative: During November 21, 2016, card C07297-K1 was used for four online purchases of $478.95, $456.96, $488.04 and $482.12 within a 30-minute window, totaling $1,906.07. The transactions were made from two different device profiles, one desktop and one mobile, and the same under-$500 run shape was observed on eleven other cards (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06881-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2) within ±30 days. This pattern matches an undocumented, coordinated scheme designed to stay just under the $500 authorization limit, a known fraud technique. Past alerts on the device profile were mostly cleared as genuine, but the repeated run shape and prior investigation linking this card to fraud point to malicious activity. The total suspicious exposure is $1,906.07. The subjects involved are the customer C07297, the primary card C07297-K1, and the connected cards listed above. The affected transactions are IDs 3476602, 3476633, 3476665 and 3476682.
